correctness.rationale: For w>=n-1 the exceptional edge is metrically redundant, reducing the finite metric to a path, whose real free space is ℓ₁^(n−1) and numerical index 1. When 0<w<n−1 every edge molecule is exposed by slopes +1 on its edge and −l_i/(L−l_i) on others; the primal ball is their signed convex hull and the dual ball is the weighted cube hyperplane ∑l_iθ_i=0. Its vertices saturate at least n−1 coordinates. The finite-dimensional real McGregor extreme-pair characterization then reduces index 1 to saturation of all dual coordinates. For odd n choose n−1 balanced unit signs, θ_n=0; even n and w>1 choose sum +1 and θ_n=−1/w; even n and 0<w<1 choose distinguished θ_n=1, n−2 balanced unit signs, final unit θ=−w. Each is a genuine interior-coordinate vertex, giving strictly smaller index. Equal weights/even n force the final sign by parity. Boundaries w=1 and w=n−1 treated explicitly. Proof applies to all reals w>0; no finite checking is substituted.
residual_risks: Applies to real scalar spaces and to one exceptional cycle weight only; it does not give actual index values below one.
